questions.prompt: Which of these are moons of Jupiter?
questions.fact: Jupiter has 95 known moons. Titan orbits Saturn, Phobos orbits Mars and Triton orbits Neptune.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries are landlocked?
questions.fact: Bolivia lost its coast to Chile in 1884 and still keeps a navy on Lake Titicaca.

questions.prompt: Which of these is the deepest ocean?
questions.fact: The Mariana Trench in the Pacific reaches about 10,935 m.

questions.prompt: Which country has the most time zones?
questions.fact: France has 12, counting its overseas territories. Russia has 11.

questions.prompt: Which planet has the shortest day?
questions.hint: The biggest one spins the fastest.
questions.fact: Jupiter spins once every 9 hours 56 minutes.

questions.prompt: How long does sunlight take to reach Earth?
questions.fact: Roughly 8 minutes 20 seconds at the speed of light.

questions.imageAlt: A star map on a dark navy sky. Seven bright stars form an hourglass shape: an orange-tinted star at the upper left shoulder, a white star at the upper right shoulder, three evenly spaced stars in a short straight diagonal line across the middle, a faint vertical trio of stars hanging just below that line, a white star at the lower left, and a large blue-white star at the lower right. Faint lines connect them into a stick figure.
questions.prompt: ANOMALY DETECTED. Our long-range scanner captured this star pattern. Name the constellation.
questions.rubric: The player must identify the constellation as Orion. Accept Orion, Orion the Hunter, or The Hunter. Naming only a part of it (Orion's Belt, the belt, the sword) or a star in it (Betelgeuse, Rigel) earns partial credit at most. Any other constellation is wrong.
questions.fact: Orion's three belt stars, Alnitak, Alnilam and Mintaka, lie 700 to 2,000 light-years away yet line up almost perfectly from Earth.
